MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  February 14, 2017

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Bucknum at 5:00 p.m., on February 14, 2017, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on February 9, 2017, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the Norman
P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Goodell
  Council Member Kelley
  Council Member Raths (arrived at 5:02 p.m.)
  Mayor Pro Tem Sachs
  Mayor Bucknum

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:01 p.m., Mayor Bucknum recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City
Council reconvened at 6:02 p.m. with all five Council Members present.

City Council Minutes  1  February 14, 2017
 CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Threat to Public Services or Facilities. Consultation with City of Mission Viejo
Emergency Operations Manager; City of Mission Viejo Cyber Security /Video Operations
Manager; City Attorney.

CS2. Conference with Legal Counsel - Existing Litigation: (Paragraph (1) of subdivision (d)
of Section 54956.9) Steven Goodridge v. City of Mission Viejo: OCSC Case No. 30-2015-
00800194-CU-EI-CJC

CS3. Conference with Real Property Negotiators. Property: APN 808-720-07, APN 808-571-
01, APN 808-720-08, APN 808-720-09, APN 808-720-10, APN 808-720-11, APN 808-720-12,
APN 808-132-16. Agency Negotiators: City Manager Wilberg; Assistant City Manager
Rattay; Community Development Director Lister; Administrative Services Director Dyas,
City Attorney. Negotiating Parties: NGP Realty. Under Negotiation: Price and Terms of
Payment.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that the City Council considered three closed session matters
and no reportable action occurred.

INVOCATION: Council Member Goodell

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Mayor Pro Tem Sachs

PRESENTATIONS

P1.  Adopted Headquarters Battalion of the 1st Marine Division Quarterly Recognition

  Mayor Bucknum presented certificates of commendation to "Noncommissioned Officer of
  the Quarter" Lance Corporal Tiesha M. Harrison and "Marine of the Quarter" Corporal
  Byron Eugene Capers.

P2.  Proclaim February 2017 as "American Heart Month" in the City of Mission Viejo

  Mayor Bucknum presented the proclamation to Suzette Ford-Duffus, Executive Director
  of the Orange County Division of the American Heart Association.

P3.  Orange County Vector Control Presentation

  The City Council Members received the presentation from Vector Control Board Member
  Dave Leckness.

City Council Minutes  2  February 14, 2017
 PUBLIC COMMENTS

Vicki Hines, M.V.: representing the Alzheimer's Association of Orange County, she provided an
overview of the Association's accomplishments in 2016.

Al Holguin, M.V.: stated that it was inappropriate for Mayor Bucknum to speak at a Christian-
based event in her official capacity. He asked that she not speak at this year’s National Day of
Prayer in her governmental role.

Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: publicly thanked the Commissioners that she appointed when she was on
the City Council for their hard work and dedication to the City of Mission Viejo.

Bob Hayes, M.V.: speaking on behalf of the Community of Character program, he announced that
the February "character movie" is A More Perfect Union. It will be shown on Sunday, February
19, at 2:00 p.m. in the Council Chamber.

Sofia Alva and Girl Scout Troop 2844, M.V.: presented their idea for a proposed Girl Scout Service
Project to provide classes for children at the City’s animal shelter, teaching responsible pet
ownership.

Rhonda Reardon, M.V.: announced that Senator Patricia Bates and Assemblyman Bill Brough will
host Senior Day at the Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center on Friday, March 10,
2017. Registration begins at 8:00 a.m. and the program will run from 9:00 to 11:00 a.m.

Helen Workun, M.V.: shared that the Mission Viejo Activities Committee is offering up to five
$1,000 scholarships for high school seniors with a volunteerism background. Applications and
additional information can be found at www.mvactivities.com and the deadline to file an
application is March 15, 2017.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

Council Member Kelley

Council Member Kelley noted that she recently heard a presentation by resident and Commissioner
Steve Spillman who has developed some very exciting conceptual plans for potential
enhancements of Oso Creek.

23.  Oso Creek Enhancements

  The City Council Members received the presentation from Steve Spillman.

  By consensus, the Council expressed that they would like to explore the concept and see
  how it might fit into the financial planning and budgeting that staff and the Council are
  currently undertaking.

City Council Minutes  3  February 14, 2017
 STAFF REPORTS

21.  Consideration of Restricting Access and Implementing a Key/Card Access System at
  La Paws Park

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay presented the staff report.

  The following presented comments in favor of a permit system at La Paws Dog Park:
  Sharon Cody, M.V.

  The following made comments in opposition to a key card system and/or in favor of
  researching the issue further: April Josephson, Rancho Santa Margarita; Nicholas Sutton
  on behalf of Nicole Sutton, M.V.; Trisa Hall, Dana Point; and Jill Rosales, M.V.

  The following presented written comments in opposition to a key card system at La Paws
  Dog Park: Joy Mortenson, M.V.; Sarah Tozki (no city of residence listed); M.L. Ibrahimi,
  M.V.; and Terry Ellen, Rancho Santa Margarita.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Goodell, to send
  this issue back to the Community Services Commission for consideration of restricted
  access using a key/card system and for a full vetting with the “Dog Park” community and
  the community at large.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, and Sachs
  NOES:  Raths
  ABSENT:  None

CONSENT CALENDAR

Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Sachs, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to approve the
Consent Calendar as outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said titles
  which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title and further
  reading waived.
City Council Minutes  4  February 14, 2017
 2.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council meeting of January 24, 2017, as
  presented.

3.  Claim Against the City - Patti Carlson & Estate of Christopher Carlson

  Rejected claim.

4.  Claim Against the City - Amon Jot, Anureet Kaur, and Kuljit Singh

  Rejected claims.

5.  Check Register Dated January 13, 2017 in the Amount of $3,287,354.31

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

6.  Check Register Dated January 20, 2017 in the Amount of $947,856.35

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

7.  Check Register Dated January 27, 2017 in the Amount of $1,338,151.06

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

8.  El Dorado Park Playground Renovations (CIP 305) - Notice of Completion

  (1) Certified the completion of and accepted the improvements for the subject project; (2)
  authorized the City Manager to sign the Notice of Completion; (3) authorized the City
  Clerk to record Notice of Completion with the County of Orange and to release the Faithful
  Performance and Payment Bonds one year and thirty-five (35) days respectively, after the
  date of recordation of the Notice of Completion contingent upon no claims or liens being
  filed with the City; and (4) authorized the payment of the final retention of $27,474.09,
  thirty-five (35) days after the date of recordation of the Notice of Completion.

9.  City Treasurer’s Monthly Report for December 2016

  Received and filed.

10.  Mission Viejo Community Development Financing  Authority  (MVCDFA)
  Treasurer’s Monthly Report for December 2016

  Received and filed.

City Council Minutes  5  February 14, 2017
 11.  Mission Viejo Housing Authority (MVHA) Treasurer’s Monthly Report for
  December 2016
  Received and filed.

12.  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency Treasurer’s Monthly
  Report for December 2016

  Received and filed.

13.  Purchase of Janitorial Related Paper, Plastic and Chemical Supplies for City Building
  Facilities

  Approved increase to Purchase Order #21700081 in the amount of $18,000.00 not to exceed
  $42,000.00 to Waxie Sanitary Supply, for Fiscal Year 2016-2017.

14.  Amendment to Agreement For Consultant Services (KNN Public Finance)

  Approved the First Amendment Consultant Services (KNN Public Finance) for public
  finance advisory services for a cumulative amount not to exceed $53,000 for services
  related to the Mission Viejo Community Development Finance Authority Variable Rate
  Demand Revenue Bonds (Mission Viejo Mall Improvement Project) 1999 Series A
  through December 31, 2019 as set forth in the Agreement.

15.  Second Amendment to Agreement For Oversight Board Legal Services (Harper &
  Burns LLP)

  Approved Second Amendment to Agreement for Oversight Board Legal Services with
  Harper & Burns LLP in an amount not to exceed $5,000 for each Annual Recognized
  Obligation Payment Schedule (ROPS) period through June 30, 2018.

16.  La Paz Bridge and Road Widening (CIP 756/761)-Railroad Agreements

  (1) Authorized the City Manager to approve the License Agreement with the Orange
  County Transportation Authority; and (2) authorized the City Manager to approve the
  Construction and Maintenance Agreement with the Southern California Regional Rail
  Authority.

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

OLD BUSINESS

17.  Third Amendment to Castlerock Environmental Inc., (Abatement) at the Marguerite
  Aquatics Complex Rehabilitation Project

City Council Minutes  6  February 14, 2017
   Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Council Member Raths, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Sachs, to ratify the
  City Manager's direction and approve Contract Amendment #3 in the amount of
  $12,727.00 to Castlerock Environmental Inc., for the removal and abatement of transite
  pipe (asbestos wrapped pipe) as part of the Marguerite Aquatics Complex Rehabilitation
  Project.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

18.  Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Mayor Pro Tem Sachs presented the report.

19.  Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  There was no report given.

20.  Orange County Sheriff’s Department (OCSD) Update

  Lt. Ken Binning provided traffic collision data for the last quarter of 2016.

STAFF REPORTS

City Attorney Curley responded to an earlier presentation during public comments and stated that
the City's participation at a National Day of Prayer event as a corporate entity, as well as the
Council Members as individuals, is not prohibited by law. Each City, public agency or
governmental entity can set its own policy and any assertion that a public agency following the
Federal lead with National Day of Prayer is not a violation. Mr. Curley stated that being elected
does not mean that one gives up their individual or constitutional rights.

City Manager Wilberg stated that he will bring to the next City Council Meeting a summary report
on the various pieces of legislation that have been introduced in Sacramento. Mayor Bucknum
asked that the presentation include information on Federal Legislation relative to Sober Living
Homes.

Mr. Wilberg also announced that the City has engaged the services of Jason Gonzales of Gonzales
and Associates as another legislative advocate, primarily to assist the City in its dispute with the
Department of Finance.
City Council Minutes  7  February 14, 2017
 COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS (Continued)

22.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities
  calendars as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk
  for the public record.

Council Member Goodell

Council Member Goodell reported that he attended a Southern California Association of
Governments (SCAG) workshop on earthquake preparedness where they conducted exercises and
learned what a city can and cannot do in an emergency. He noted that the City of Mission Viejo
does not own the hospital, schools, or utilities so the best approach is to work closely with the
other agencies to prepare. Council Member Goodell said he learned that there is a 280-mile section
of the Pacific Plate that hasn't moved in a very long time and some day that piece will not hold any
longer and the “big one” will hit. Because all three of the aquifers serving Southern California
cross that fault, he said there will be major problems. Council Member Goodell noted that staff
member Paul Catsimanes will be preparing a report and a plan for the Council to consider so the
City can be as prepared as possible for its residents.

Council Member Kelley

Council Member Kelley announced that on January 27 she attended the South Orange County
Economic Coalition meeting where several of the local city managers were in attendance providing
updates on their cities. She said that Mission Viejo's City Manager, Dennis Wilberg, gave the best
presentation and she was very proud to say that she is from Mission Viejo. Council Member Kelley
announced that Mission Viejo Television (MVTV) is airing a three-part special featuring the
Marching Band programs at the City’s local high schools. The show is airing daily at 3:30 p.m. on
Cox Channel 30 and ATT&T Uverse Channel 99. Regarding the National Day of Prayer event,
Council Member Kelley stated that she too attended and she was glad to see Mayor Bucknum
there. She said the event draws many, many churches and people and she looks forward to
attending again this year. In closing, Council Member Kelley reminded residents that the character
movie for this month of “unity” is A More Perfect Union and it will be shown in the Council
Chamber on Sunday, February 19 at 2:00 p.m.

Council Member Raths

Council Member Raths had no comments.

Mayor Pro Tem Sachs

Mayor Pro Tem Sachs thanked Council Member Goodell for the information he provided on
earthquake preparedness and stated that he looks forward to keeping an eye on the legislation that
City Manager Wilberg mentioned earlier. He discussed the concept of state mandates and retention
City Council Minutes  8  February 14, 2017
 of local control and stated that the City needs to pay attention in this area. Mayor Pro Tem Sachs
said that he'd like to see Mission Viejo take a leadership position in managing these issues so the
residents are protected.

Mayor Bucknum

Mayor Bucknum discussed the Oroville Dam situation and noted that the State has known about
issues with the dam for 12 years. She said that she is passionate about Mission Viejo taking care
of its infrastructure and the Oroville situation brought to light that the State has focused on other
issues and, as a result, has put human life in danger. Mayor Bucknum said that Mission Viejo
Council Members will continue to serve on regional boards to make sure that the City’s voice is
heard. She thanked Elks Lodge 244 for recently honoring public safety officers and she reminded
residents of several upcoming events including the town hall meeting on public safety on February
27, 2017, from 6:00 to 7:00 p.m.; a Wounded Warriors baseball game at Saddleback College on
March 25, hosted by Assemblyman Bill Brough and Senator Pat Bates; and an interfaith Law
Enforcement Appreciation Day at Melinda Park on Saturday, February 21 from 11:00 a.m. to 1:00
p.m. In closing, Mayor Bucknum recognized Tesoro High School choir teacher Keith Hancock
who is the recipient of the 2017 Music Educator Award/Grammy.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 8:54 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Bucknum adjourned the meeting to Tuesday, February 28, 2017, at 5:00 p.m.

______________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of February 28, 2017

City Council Minutes  9  February 14, 2017
